'''Bryant McFadden''' (born November 21, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State Seminoles]] and was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the second round of the [[2005 NFL draft]]. McFadden was also a member of the [[Arizona Cardinals]]. He earned two [[Super Bowl ring]]s during his time with the Steelers, [[Super Bowl XL]] and [[Super Bowl XLIII]].
McFadden currently serves as a studio analyst for the all-digital sports network, 120 Sports. He also hosts Huddlecast, the football podcast of his alma mater, Florida State University, and co-hosts All Things Covered, a podcast with former NFL cornerback [[Patrick Peterson]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://thehuddlenetwork.com/go/about-the-huddle-network/|title=About THN – The Huddle Network|website=thehuddlenetwork.com|access-date=June 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190128082910/http://thehuddlenetwork.com/go/about-the-huddle-network/|archive-date=January 28, 2019|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

'''Bryan Johnson''' (born January 18, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[fullback (American football)|fullback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] a [[linebacker]] for the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos]]. He entered the NFL as an [[undrafted free agent]] in the 2000 when he signed with the [[Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Haugh |first=David |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2004-10-12-0410120268-story.html |title=The Bears' Bryan Johnson is grateful to former scout Melvin Bratton, who knew where the ex-Boise State linebacker belonged |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=October 12, 2004 |accessdate=August 12, 2023 }}</ref> In 2004, he was traded to the [[Chicago Bears]] as a pending restricted free agent.<ref>{{cite news |last=Haugh |first=David |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2004-03-29-0403290377-story.html |title=Bears to land fullback in trade |work=Chicago Tribune |date=March 29, 2004 |accessdate=August 12, 2023 }}</ref>  Johnson attended [[Highland High School (Pocatello, Idaho)|Highland High School]] in [[Pocatello, Idaho]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pocatello's Johnson bidding for Redskins' fullback job |url=https://www.lmtribune.com/sports/pocatellos-johnson-bidding-for-redskins-fullback-job-0e8f96e0 |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=The Lewiston Tribune |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Big-league guy visits small-town kids |url=https://www.lmtribune.com/northwest/big-league-guy-visits-small-town-kids-7a970332 |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=The Lewiston Tribune |language=en}}</ref>

In Bears training camp in 2006 he tore part of his hamstring and had surgery a few days later.  Johnson retired from the NFL in 2007 after being on injured reserve for his last season.
